sections.h2: Where is Grady County and which towns sit inside it?
sections.html:
Grady County lies along Georgia's southern border with Florida, and Cairo is both its seat and its largest city. The General Assembly created it on August 17, 1905, from parts of Decatur and Thomas counties, and named it for Henry W. Grady, the editor of the Atlanta Constitution (Wikipedia).

The county covers 460 square miles, of which 455 are land. Most of it drains to the upper Ochlockonee River, the northwest corner reaches the Flint River basin, and part of the Red Hills Region falls inside the line. Mitchell County is the neighbor to the north, Thomas to the east, Decatur to the west, and Leon and Gadsden counties in Florida touch the south and southwest.

Cairo and Whigham are the two incorporated cities. Calvary is a census-designated place, and Beachton and Spence are unincorporated communities. Grady County Schools runs six public schools, Cairo High School among them. A house in any of these places is billed through the county tax commissioner, and a city can add its own levy on top, so read every line of the bill before you sign a sale contract.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Grady County homes?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 26,236 residents in the county, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 26,590, a rise of 1.4% over the estimates base. Persons 65 and older make up 21.2% of the population, which matters because age-based exemptions are among the first things an older owner should check before listing.

The QuickFacts poverty rate for the county is 19.5%. Where an owner has fallen behind on a bill, a plain conversation with the tax commissioner about the balance usually comes before any listing decision (QuickFacts).

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Grady County?
sections.html:
Two offices split the work. The tax commissioner bills and collects real property, personal property, motor vehicle, mobile home and timber tax. The Tax Assessor office, headed by a chief appraiser, handles returns, conservation and agricultural applications, and the homestead paperwork described on the county's assessor page.

  • Tax commissioner (qPublic site): 114 1st Street NE, Cairo, GA 39828, property phone 229-377-3322, open 7:30 AM to 6:00 PM Monday through Thursday and closed Friday.
  • County services pages for the tax commissioner and the assessor: 33 17th Avenue NW, Cairo, GA 39827, weekdays 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
  • Parcel search: the Grady County tax commissioner site carries a property search for any parcel in the county.

The two county pages print different addresses and hours. Call 229-377-3322 before you drive to pay in person, and ask which door takes the payment you are bringing. The county's tax commissioner page and its assessor page are the places to look for updates.

sections.h2: How does a Grady County assessment notice and appeal work?
sections.html:
Georgia sets assessed value at 40% of fair market value as of January 1, and the Board of Tax Assessors mails a notice each year. If you disagree with the fair market value shown, send a written appeal to that board, postmarked no later than 45 days after the mailing date of the notice. The state form for this is PT-311A, and the appeal must say whether you want the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or an arbitrator (Georgia Department of Revenue FAQ).

Grady County had an unusual cycle in 2024. A revaluation ran late, notices went out in September, and the county told owners that some 45-day windows would end October 28 and others October 31. The county also said the digest would reach the tax commissioner late and that commissioners expected a significant drop in the millage rate once values were reset (county notice).

The lesson for a seller is to keep the notice. A buyer's lender, or a title company working through a payoff, may ask which value the current bill rests on, and an open appeal changes how the bill is read.

sections.h2: When are Grady County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The statewide default due date is December 20, and the Department of Revenue's county facts page notes that a governing authority may move it to December 1 or November 15, or bill in installments. Grady County's bill prints the date that applies to you. Each taxpayer has 60 days from the postmark date of the bill before interest begins to build, and penalties can follow on unpaid balances (Grady County property tax facts).

Ask the commissioner's office for the exact penalty and interest figures on an overdue parcel rather than relying on a general rule. Other fixed points in the state calendar apply here too:

  • Property tax returns are filed between January 1 and April 1 each year.
  • Owners of a mobile home in the county on January 1 return it for tax by April 1, at the same time they apply for the location permit.
  • A refund claim for tax that was erroneously or illegally assessed must start within three years of payment.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and special assessments can Grady County owners claim?
sections.html:
A homestead application can be filed at any time after the home becomes your primary residence, up to and including April 1 of the first year you want the exemption. The assessor's page cites Georgia code section 48-5-44. The Department of Revenue states that failing to apply counts as a waiver. The state's standard homestead deduction is $2,000 off assessed value, and the Department's county page for Grady lists no local homestead exemptions beyond the statewide ones. That page carries a 2016 date, so ask the assessor whether anything has been added since.

Early in 2025 the county posted a notice that its commissioners intended to opt out of the statewide adjusted base year homestead exemption, with hearings held on February 17 and 18, 2025. Ask the assessor how the freeze rules apply to your home before you assume a lower bill follows you to the next owner.

  • Conservation use or preferential agricultural assessment: file between January 1 and April 1.
  • Freeport exemption on commercial and industrial inventory: available only where local voters approved it, filed with the assessors on the return schedule.
  • A new owner must apply in their own name; an exemption does not transfer with the deed.

sections.h2: What did Grady County's 2026 millage notice say?
sections.html:
A county notice posted in November 2026 said the Board of Commissioners had tentatively adopted a rate that required a property tax increase of 4.72 percent. The notice printed a tentative county rate of 12.64 mills, an increase of .57 mills, and said that without the increase the rate would be no more than 12.070 mills. Three public hearings were scheduled that month at 33 17th Avenue NW in Cairo (county notice).

This figure covers the county government levy only. School and city rates are set separately, and the final numbers appear on the bill. Ask the commissioner's office for the adopted rates when you need a payoff figure.

sections.h2: How should a Grady County seller handle tax at closing?
sections.html:
Whoever owned the property on January 1 owes the whole year's ad valorem tax. The Department of Revenue says Georgia law gives no refund for a partial year, even to an owner who sells on January 2. The buyer and seller therefore divide the bill in the sales contract, and the settlement statement should show who pays what.

  • Call the tax commissioner and ask for the balance due on the parcel for the current and any earlier years.
  • Say so if an assessment appeal is still open, so the closing agent can plan for a changed final figure.
  • Give the closing agent the payoff amount and the office that will receive it.
  • Tell the office when an exemption no longer applies because you have moved out.

A buyer who purchases as-is for cash still inherits the same parcel record, so back taxes are best cleared on the settlement statement instead of left for later.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Grady County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Go to the tax commissioner's office in Cairo. The tax commissioner's own site lists 114 1st Street NE, Cairo, GA 39828, with hours from 7:30 AM to 6:00 PM Monday through Thursday and closed Fridays, while the county's services page lists 33 17th Avenue NW with weekday hours of 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Call 229-377-3322 to confirm which location takes your payment.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Grady County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the mailing date of the assessment notice, and the written appeal must be postmarked within that window. File it with the Board of Tax Assessors, using the state's PT-311A form, and choose the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or an arbitrator.

faqs.q: Does Grady County have local homestead exemptions?
faqs.a: The Department of Revenue's county facts page says no local homestead exemptions were offered when it was published in 2016, and only the statewide ones were open. The county's 2025 notice about opting out of the adjusted base year exemption means you should also ask the assessor which freeze rules apply to your home today.

faqs.q: Who owes the tax if I sell my Grady County house after January 1?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is liable for the full year, and Georgia allows no refund for a partial year. In practice the contract and settlement statement divide the bill between buyer and seller, so confirm the amount with the tax commissioner before closing.

faqs.q: Can I get a refund of Grady County tax I overpaid?
faqs.a: Yes, if the tax was erroneously or illegally assessed and collected. Put the request in writing and start it within three years of the payment date. When an assessment is under appeal, any refund is processed automatically once the final taxable value is set.
